theEnumerationDefect.summary: check-c2-v7.py's candidate totality was built from two walkers, _integer_leaf_steps and _number_leaf_steps, each of which named the JSON type it covered. theEnumerationDefect.thePattern: This is the third consecutive version whose retained residual pointed exactly one JSON type away from the live hazard. v5's pointed at gate dominance while the live hazard was the taint model; v6's blind spot named strings while the live hazard was floats; v7's RES-C2V7-07 names strings while the live hazard is booleans. The cause is structural and not editorial: a totality that enumerates WHICH TYPES IT COVERS is a list of places, and the defect moves to a place not on the list. That is the failure v6 was authored to escape at the COMPARISON layer, where it stopped patching operators and built a primitive; it reappeared at the ENUMERATION layer. The repair is therefore not a boolean walker, because a boolean walker would leave the same structure in place with one more entry in it.

theSkeletonDefect.summary: check-c2-v8.py bound the SHAPE of its candidate through document_skeleton, which hashed _steps_text(steps) -- a slash-join with no escaping. The map from a structural path to its text is not injective, so document_skeleton({'a': {'b': 1}}) and document_skeleton({'a': {}, 'a/b': 1}) are the same list and their digests are equal. Everything else in the totality is unaffected: a leaf moved is still one leaf of the same type and its old and new parents are both still containers, so every node, container and per-type leaf count is identical too. It is not a defect in the leaf census, which reached the node, nor in the primitive, which was never applied to the path. The defect is that a HUMAN-READABLE RENDERING was used as an IDENTITY, which is the same class as using == on two numbers: one representation standing in for another where the substitution loses information.
theSkeletonDefect.thePattern: Every version of this lineage has failed at a joint where one representation stands in for another and the substitution is not injective. v6: 1.0 == 1, two values and one truth. v7: a duplicate key, two leaves and one object. v8: a boolean leaf, a type off the list. v9: 'a/b', two paths and one string. The v8 reviewer put it exactly: derive-vs-enumerate holds over the TYPE dimension and not over the IDENTITY dimension. A totality that REACHES every node and then cannot tell two nodes apart binds the shape of a document other than the one in front of it. The repair is therefore not an escaping rule for slashes, because an escaping rule is a list of characters and the defect moves to a character not on the list. It is the primitive that is already proven injective by the existence of its inverse.

thePrimitive.why: Every repair before v6 guarded call sites. v4 guarded the wire validator and left its census bare; v5 guarded the census and left its own repro enumeration bare. thePrimitive.whatItIs: jx_canon, a total, length-framed, type-tagged canonical encoding of a JSON value, and everything else defined in terms of it. Comparison, ordering, membership, key lookup, set algebra, dedup, sorting and extremes are all decided by STRING equality or STRING ordering over canonical tokens. v8 adds jx_loads, the PARSE, to the same block: the boundary at which the bytes become a value is a law-18 gate like any other, and an adopter who copies the block gets it rather than having to remember it.
thePrimitive.whyItIsSoundAndNotJustCareful: jx_canon is INVERTIBLE. jx_decanon reconstructs the original value exactly, type and all, which means jx_canon is injective, which means it can never give two distinct JSON values the same token. That is executed over the whole corpus on every run and the counts are published: corpus values, distinct tokens and round trips must all agree.
thePrimitive.theOperatorSpace: Equality, inequality and their operator.* call forms; ordering in both directions and their call forms; membership and non-membership over lists, tuples, sets and dict keys; key lookup by subscript, get, pop, setdefault and fromkeys; set algebra including subset, superset, disjointness, union, intersection and difference; dedup through set(), frozenset(), set literals and set and dict comprehensions; aggregation through sorted, min, max, sum and Counter; container equality at any depth, where [1] equals [1.0] and an object with an integer value equals the same object with the float; boolean-as-integer, where hash(True) equals hash(1); signed zero; foreign numeric types that compare equal to an integer; BARE TRUTHINESS, where bool(1), bool(1.0) and bool(True) are all the same value so `if x:` carries exactly the equivalence semantics this table exists to enumerate; %d STRINGIFICATION; and THE PARSE, where json.loads keeps the last duplicate key, accepts NaN and Infinity, and turns `-0` into 0 and `1E2` into 100.0. The last three groups are v8's: the truthiness and stringification rows were omitted from v6's table, which called itself the operator space, and the parse rows are IR-C2V6-01. Every row carries a live demonstration that the host-language hazard still reproduces AND a demonstration that the primitive answers differently, and both are executed on every run.
thePrimitive.whyTheContainerHalfMatters: hash(1), hash(1.0) and hash(True) are equal, so len({1, 1.0, True}) is 1. Three distinct JSON values silently become one, and a cardinality published from that set is a false measurement that no equality guard would ever see. This is why the repair could not be a wider list of comparison operators.
thePrimitive.shouldACheckerCompareAMeasuredValueAgain: The comparison exists to catch contract drift and it is also what creates the false-accept surface. v8 keeps the comparison and removes the surface: jx_bind asserts the JSON type of each side independently and FIRST, then compares canonical strings. No numeric operator runs, so there is no coercion path to defend. The residual risk is no longer numeric; it is that the measurement function measures the wrong space, which is RES-C2V6-04 and is a different failure mode.
thePrimitive.whatThePrimitiveCannotDo: It canonicalises a value it is GIVEN, and v8 moves the boundary of that sentence rather than repeating it. thePrimitive.orderingAndEqualityAgree: v6's jx_order reported EQUAL for 0.0 against -0.0 and for NaN against every float, both of which jx_equal calls distinct, and v6 disclosed only the equality half of that divergence. v8 does not disclose the ordering half; it removes it. jx_order decides the equal case by the same canonical string comparison jx_equal uses, before any < runs, and returns None - not comparable - for two distinct values of the same JSON type that do not order, which after this change is NaN and only NaN. The agreement is measured over the whole corpus cross-product on every run and published as primitiveOrderEqualityDivergences.
thePrimitive.howToStateTheNumericPropertyCorrectly: STATED ACCURATELY BECAUSE BOTH v6 DOCUMENTS STATED IT WRONGLY. v6 claimed 'no numeric operator is ever executed on a wire operand'. That is false as worded: jx_order runs `a < b` and jx_int_in_range runs `low <= value <= high`. The property that is true, and that is the one doing the work, is that NO COMPARISON BETWEEN OPERANDS OF DIFFERENT JSON TYPE IS EVER EXECUTED. Both of those functions gate every operand to the same JSON type FIRST, so no coercion path is reachable; `<` between two values already proved to be JSON integers cannot coerce anything. Equality never runs a numeric operator at all - it is string equality over canonical tokens.
thePrimitive.whatTheAdoptionStepsUsedToSayAndWhyThatM: v6's step 3 told an adopter to call jx_min and jx_max, NEITHER OF WHICH EXISTED anywhere in check-c2-v6.py, so following the normative instructions verbatim produced a NameError; and both v6 documents attributed to jx_sorted a refusal of heterogeneous JSON type sets that it does not perform - it orders them, and jx_sorted_homogeneous is the function that refuses. Adoption is one of this artifact's two declared deliverables, so a wrong adoption step is a live defect and not a typo. Both are fixed by construction here: jx_min and jx_max now exist and are real replacements for min and max rather than aliases for jx_sorted, the refusal is attributed to the functions that perform it, and check-c2-v9.py reads every jx_ name out of its own docstring AND out of this document on every run and emits a named finding for any that it does not define.
thePrimitive.theIdentityIsAGateToo: IR-C2V8-01. jx_canon was built to decide whether two VALUES are the same value. v8 used it for exactly that and then identified a node's PATH with a slash-join of its steps, which is not injective, so the layer that binds the document's shape could not tell ['a','b'] from ['a/b']. The lesson generalises past this artifact: ANY place a checker substitutes a human-readable rendering for a structural identity is the same defect as ==. The repair is to route the path through the same single decision point as the value -- jx_canon of the steps LIST -- and to keep the rendering strictly for finding text a human reads. An adopter should treat this as the third gate beside the comparison and the parse: if you hash a path, a key, a name or any other identity, hash jx_canon of its structure, and prove injectivity by exhibiting the inverse rather than by arguing that collisions are unlikely.
thePrimitive.theEnumerationIsAGateToo: IR-C2V7-01. The primitive decides whether two values are comparable and whether they are equal. It cannot decide WHICH VALUES ARE PUT TO IT, and in v7 that decision was made by two hand-written walkers that named the JSON types they covered. The set of leaves under the primitive is a gate like any other, so the walk that produces it lives inside the primitive and derives its coverage from the type space rather than from a list: jx_leaf_census names the two container cases and nothing else, and jx_type_space measures that every member of the RFC 8259 value space, under the one declared refinement of number, is reached. documentSkeleton.rule: The PATH and the JSON TYPE of every NODE of this document, container nodes included, canonicalised and hashed into one digest. The path is bound as jx_canon of the STEPS LIST, not as a rendering of it: v8 hashed a slash-join with no escaping, ['a','b'] and ['a/b'] produced the same text, and one contiguous eleven-byte edit reparenting a narrative leaf left this digest and every count below byte-identical under a full green banner (IR-C2V8-01). jx_canon is length-framed and type-tagged and jx_decanon inverts it, so two distinct paths cannot share one identity and an array index cannot be confused with an object key of the same spelling. Values are deliberately absent, which is what makes this a fixpoint: publishing the digest inside the document it describes cannot change what it describes. So a string leaf, a null leaf, a renamed key, a REPARENTED key or subtree, a retyped leaf or an EMPTY array or object -- which holds no leaf for any census, however total, to reach -- cannot be added, removed, moved or changed without a named finding. subtrees carries the same digest per ROOT SUBTREE, so a shape change is additionally named at the region that contains it rather than only at a digest over the whole document; the exposure that leaves is RES-C2V9-17.

v9MeasuredCountersRule: EVERY LEAF OF THIS DOCUMENT IS UNDER THREE OBLIGATIONS AT ONCE, the first of them names no JSON type, and the second of them now binds an IDENTITY rather than a rendering. VALUE: every leaf whose JSON type is ruled BIND -- null, boolean, integer and number -- is bound to a value this run measured or to a byte of a hash-verified pinned input; a leaf no layer binds is itself a named finding, so narrowing the binding table fails closed. SHAPE: the path and the JSON type of every node of this document, container nodes included, are hashed into documentSkeleton and bound, so adding, removing, renaming, REPARENTING or retyping any node is a named finding whatever its type and whether or not its value is bound. The path is hashed as jx_canon of the STEPS LIST. v8 hashed a slash-join of the steps, which is not injective, and one contiguous eleven-byte edit moved a narrative leaf across a slash boundary with this digest and every count below byte-identical, exit 0 and a full green banner: IR-C2V8-01. documentSkeleton.subtrees carries the same digest per ROOT SUBTREE so that a shape change is named at a region and not only at a digest over the whole document. POPULATION: the per-type leaf counts are published and bound. The type coverage of the first obligation is not enumerated anywhere: jx_leaf_census names the two CONTAINER cases and lets every other JSON type fall through, jx_type_space measures which types that fall-through reaches over a witness corpus required to realise every member of the declared type space AND AT EVERY DEPTH OF A DECLARED LADDER, census_walk_agreement measures the census against the node walk over THIS document at every depth it actually has, the declared type space is required to be exactly the RFC 8259 value space under one declared refinement of number and the production table is required to equal what PARSING a corpus of JSON texts realises, and a leaf whose type carries no disposition rule is a named finding rather than a silent pass. residuals.title: the type space is anchored to a DECLARED table of the standard's productions, and that one table is not executable
residuals.detail: THIS IS THE SHARPEST ATTACK ON THE IR-C2V7-01 REPAIR AND IT IS WRITTEN HERE RATHER THAN LEFT FOR A REVIEWER TO FIND. The totality itself names no JSON type: jx_leaf_census names the two container cases and lets everything else fall through, so it cannot be narrower than the set of types a document can hold. But the DISPOSITION of a leaf is looked up in LEAF_TYPE_RULES, which is a seven-row table, and that table's completeness is established by comparison against JX_TYPES and JX_RFC8259_PRODUCTIONS, which are also declared tables. Four of the five links in that chain are EXECUTED and measured on every run: LEAF_TYPE_RULES must equal the leaf/container split jx_type_space MEASURES by running the census over witnesses; every member of JX_TYPES must be realised by a witness; every member must refine some declared production; every production must refine into declared types; and no type may be both a leaf and a container. The link that is NOT executable is the last one: that RFC 8259 sections 3 to 7 define exactly seven value productions and no eighth. That sentence is read from the standard by a human and transcribed into JX_RFC8259_PRODUCTIONS. MEASURED BOUNDARY: primitiveTypeSpaceRfcProductions productions, one declared refinement (number into integer and number), primitiveTypeSpaceWitnesses witnesses, primitiveTypeSpaceDeclaredTypes declared types of which primitiveTypeSpaceUnwitnessedTypes are unwitnessed, and primitiveTypeSpaceAdmissions types that are neither a leaf nor a container. Every one of those is published and bound. The unexecutable link is exactly one transcription of one sentence of one standard. v9 NARROWS THIS AND DOES NOT CLOSE IT. The v8 reviewer measured that a bogus eighth production -- ('date', ('string',)) -- produced ZERO findings from leaf_rule_findings, because a refinement into an already-declared type narrows nothing, while REMOVING a production was caught semantically. What contained the widening direction was primitiveTypeSpaceRfcProductions, a count. Both directions are semantic now: jx_rfc_production_space dispatches each text of a declared JSON GRAMMAR CORPUS on its first significant byte, exactly as RFC 8259's own grammar does, PARSES it, and the production table is required to equal that measurement in both directions. 'date' dispatches to no production and is named. What is still declared, and why this stays RETAINED-OPEN, is that the corpus covers the grammar: a production of the standard for which this corpus holds no witness is invisible to the measurement and to the table alike. The v8 reviewer called this residual the first in the lineage that names the real hazard rather than one type away from it, and said it slightly understates itself; it is retained in those terms and its status is now gated in both directions by a declared open set, because in v8 one edit downgraded it to RETAINED and reached a fully green run.
residuals.whyNotClosed: A checker cannot execute a standards document. The alternatives are worse rather than better: deriving the production set from the host parser would anchor the type space to CPython's json module, which is the very thing IR-C2V6-01 showed is not a trustworthy authority about JSON; and deriving it from the type space would be circular. What can be done is to make every OTHER link executable, publish the figures, and say plainly which single link is not - which is what this residual does. Naming it is not closing it.
residuals.whatStandsInFrontOfIt: the fall-through construction of jx_leaf_census, which does not consult any of these tables and reports a leaf of ANY type including one no table names; the C2V9-LEAFRULE finding, which fires on a leaf whose type carries no disposition rule, so an unanticipated type is a named finding rather than a silent pass even if every table above is wrong about it; and the live injection probe, which puts a witness of every declared type into the candidate at unbound paths on every run and requires each to be named.

That closes the widening direction the v8 reviewer measured open. What remains declared is that this corpus of primitiveTypeSpaceGrammarTexts texts covers the grammar -- an eighth production of the standard that this corpus has no witness for would be invisible to both halves. RETAINED-OPEN.

The type space itself is no longer sampled over DEPTH: jx_type_space measures at primitiveTypeSpacePlacements placements down a declared ladder, and census_walk_agreement compares the census against the node walk at all censusWalkLeaves leaf positions of this document with censusLeavesAgreed agreeing. residuals.detail: OBS-C2V8-02 measured that v8's claim -- 'every residual carries a MEASURED BOUNDARY clause citing bound counters' -- was false by one and arguably two, that RES-C2V8-11 carried no such clause and cited zero counters while stating its figures as prose words, and that NOTHING IN THE CHECKER ENFORCED THE CLAUSE: _residual_findings required only that whyNotClosed be forty characters long, and the string 'MEASURED BOUNDARY' occurred nowhere in check-c2-v8.py.
